titles.title: HalfLife1
titles.engine: GoldSrc, WON Half-Life 1.1.0.8 (GOTY tree). hl.exe is the 942,080-byte WON launcher (PE 2001-09-11). It owns the mode list and the mode switch; hw.dll/sw.dll are the engine. The banner reads 'Half-Life 45/1.1.0.8 (hw build 1792)', network protocol 45.
titles.launch_sets: 1280x960 fullscreen OpenGL on every 1080p LCD. All five launchers (Half-Life, Opposing Force, Blue Shift, Team Fortress Classic and Deathmatch Classic .bat) run `call FLEETRES.BAT` and then `hl.exe -nosierra -full -gl -w %FR_W43% -h %FR_H43% -toconsole [-game x]`. FR_W43/FR_H43 is the largest classic 4:3 mode the driver offers: GAMERES reports four_three=1280x960 on .123, .145, .195 and .240 (read 2026-09-29 00:09). The launcher looks up -w/-h exactly in its 4:3-only list; with no match it takes the last entry of the same width, and failing that index 0 (400x300). Measured: 1280x960 on .123 and .240 (2026-08-31, screenshots) and on .246, now .195 (DISPLAYCFG). The mechanism is present and correct in the tree: FLEETRES.EXE md5 bb180f3b… matches provisioning/fleetres, FLEETRES.BAT is identical across titles, and `stage-fleetres.py --check` lists these launchers as current. GAMERES has no HalfLife1 rule (it is a command-line title). One latent defect: the CounterStrike16 GAMERES rule writes EngineModeW/H=1920x1080, and only this WON launcher reads those values; that is the live value on all four LCD boxes. Through the .bat launchers it does no harm, because -w/-h override it (0x413d21-0x413dbe). A bare `hl.exe` start would fall to 400x300. The panel scaler decides whether the 4:3 image is pillarboxed or stretched.
titles.menu_source:
The list is the WON launcher's Configuration > Video > 'Video modes' (UTF-16 resources 'Video &modes', 'Mode List' and 'Test video mode'; class CVideoModeDlg). It is built at VA 0x413b90 from two sources:
(1) A hardcoded table at file offset 0xcef70: 400x300, 512x384, 640x480, 800x600, 1024x768, 1152x864, 1280x960.
(2) IDirectDraw::EnumDisplayModes. The callback at VA 0x413a20 keeps a mode only if height/width equals 0.75 exactly (the double 0.75 at VA 0x4ae078, fidiv/fcomp), height <= 1024 (cmp esi,0x400), width >= 400 (cmp ebp,0x190) and the bpp matches.
So a 16:9 mode can never enter the list. Computed from each box's driver mode list:
- .123/.145: 640x480, 800x600, 1024x768, 1152x864, 1280x960
- .195: 640x480, 800x600, 1024x768, 1280x960
- .240: 400x300 up to 1280x960
The official WON 1.1.1.0 patch is on the share. I inflated its hl.exe (2002-06-06) from the Wise installer: it has the same 0.75 test and the same height cap, and only adds 1600x1200 to the table.

- goldsrc_registry_value_matrix.txt: WON hl.exe reads EngineModeW/H/BPP/Windowed, EngineType, EngineGLDriver and LauncherWidth/Height. It reads no ScreenWidth (checked case-insensitively, ASCII and UTF-16).
- probe_123.json, probe_145.json, probe_195.json, probe_240.json: GAMERES mode lists, plus HKCU\Software\Valve\Half-Life\Settings showing EngineModeW=1920, EngineModeH=1080 and LauncherWidth=640 (1280 on .195).
- Staged files read: HalfLife1/Half-Life.bat and the four sibling .bat files (FR_W43/FR_H43), HOW-TO-RUN.txt (the .240 measurement: -w 1920 -h 1080 gave a 400x300 desktop, -w 1280 -h 960 gave 1280x960), version.txt 1.1.0.8, install.reg (EngineModeW/H 0x400/0x300).
- Earlier frames: .claude/worktrees/perbox/evidence/123_HalfLife1_Half-Life.png and 240_HalfLife1_Half-Life.png (1280x960).
titles.fix:
No configuration or registry change can do it: the 16:9 rejection is compiled into this WON hl.exe, and the 1.1.1.0 patch has the same filter. The honest state is the one already applied: 1280x960 4:3 via FR_W43/FR_H43, with the panel or driver scaler set to preserve aspect.
The only real route to 1920x1080 in a menu is to re-stage the Half-Life, TFC and DMC content onto the Steam-era GoldSrc build 4554 that CounterStrike16 already stages. Its GameUI shows 1920 x 1080 under Aspect Ratio 'Widescreen', and CounterStrike16's 'Play Half-Life Deathmatch.bat' already runs `-game valve` on that engine at %FR_W%x%FR_H%. That is a staging job for the build VM, not a config edit.
Not recommended: hex-patching WON hl.exe (the je at file offset 0x13a4d and the cmp esi,0x400 at 0x13a53). It is untested, how hw.dll build 1792 behaves at 16:9 is unknown, and it alters a vendor binary.
Related cleanup for the later phase: agent/shared/gameres.h's CounterStrike16 rows should stop writing the WON-only EngineMode*/EngineType/EngineGLDriver values at the widescreen pair. Either move EngineModeW/H to a HalfLife1 rule at %W43%/%H43% or drop them, and correct the comments that call this 'one shared value pair'.
titles.fix_source: The 4:3 answer is already in the tree. The Steam-era engine is already on the share at Games-Library/CounterStrike16 (hl.exe, hw.dll build 4554, valve/cl_dlls/gameui.dll). The HL content is in Games-Library/HalfLife1 and on the retail ISOs under Files/Games/Windows XP/Half-Life GOTY + Opposing Force + Blue Shift/. Files/Game Updates/halflife-1.1.1.0-english.exe was checked and does not help. Nothing needs downloading.
titles.fix_risk:
- Keeping 4:3: none.
- Re-staging onto build 4554: high. WON-era game and client DLL compatibility (single player, TFC, DMC), savegames and the RevEmu environment are all unverified. The protocol moves from 45 to 48, which breaks LAN with boxes still on the WON tree but reaches the fleet HLDS. Opposing Force and Blue Shift stay broken for their own reasons.
- gameres.h cleanup: low, since the .bat already overrides those values.
- Hex patch: high.
titles.hw_check:
Use an XP LCD box (.145 or .123), where SCREENSHOT 0 captures fullscreen GoldSrc.
1. `EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\HalfLife1" "Half-Life.bat"` brings up the engine console fullscreen.
2. `DISPLAYCFG get` should show live 1280x960.
3. `UIKEY ESCAPE` opens the WON shell. The shell runs at LauncherWidth x LauncherHeight: 640x480 on .123/.145/.240, 1280x960 on .195.
4. Configuration > Video > Video modes, then SCREENSHOT 0. The list should end at 1280x960 with no 1920x1080.
The console is proven keyboard-drivable (UIKEY TEXT). The VGUI1 shell buttons should take absolute UICLICK (it follows the OS cursor), but that is unverified; if clicks do not land, a person has to do this once.
Afterwards run `taskkill /f /im "hl.exe"` and confirm the desktop is back at 1920x1080.
titles.verifier_notes:
- The menu contents come from disassembly plus each box's EnumDisplaySettings list (GAMERES). The WON launcher enumerates through DirectDraw at 16 bpp unless -24bpp/-32bpp is given, so the exact low end may differ slightly; the 4:3 filter cannot be escaped.
- Generator drift: the HalfLife1 recipe in scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py still substitutes '-w %FR_W% -h %FR_H%' into an unpatched launcher. Re-staging an old launcher would bring back the 400x300 bug. The staged .bat files are correct (FR_W43), and --check passes only because the call block is already present.
- Opposing Force and Blue Shift are broken independently of resolution (KNOWN-BROKEN-bshift-and-gearbox.txt).

titles.title: CounterStrike16
titles.engine: GoldSrc Steam-era build 4554: Counter-Strike 1.6 No-Steam V42 by ZCP (2009) with RevEmu 9.80. hw.dll is 1,840,440 bytes (PE 2009-06-15); valve/cl_dlls/gameui.dll is dated 2009-04-27. Network protocol 48.
titles.launch_sets:
1920x1080 fullscreen OpenGL on every 1080p LCD. 'Play Counter-Strike.bat' runs `call FLEETRES.BAT` and then `hl.exe -game cstrike -full -gl -w %FR_W% -h %FR_H%`; FR_W/FR_H is 1920x1080 on .123, .145, .195 and .240.
CVideoMode_Common::Init (hw.dll VA 0x1dc6860) works like this:
1. It reads ScreenWidth/ScreenHeight/ScreenBPP (defaults 640/480/16).
2. -width/-w and -height/-h override those values.
3. It takes the exact mode if it is in the enumerated list. Otherwise it takes the last entry of the same width, then index 0 (640x480). -forceres only applies in windowed mode.
4. It writes the chosen mode back to ScreenWidth/Height.
1920x1080 is in the list on all four boxes, so the command line wins.
Measured: 1920x1080 fullscreen on .123 (2026-08-31: main menu, and in-game on the fleet server) and on .240. On .246 (now .195) it runs at 1920x1080, but Win7 cannot photograph the fullscreen surface.
The mechanism is present and correct in the tree (FLEETRES md5 matches the repo). The comments in install.reg and gameres.h say 'CS ignores -w/-h'. The binary disagrees: the 08-31 1080p pass predates GAMERES, when the key still held 4:3 values. GAMERES's ScreenWidth/Height=1920x1080 write (the live value on all four boxes) is therefore redundant for this launcher.
titles.menu_source:
Driver-enumerated, then filtered, in two layers.
Engine list: the IDirectDraw::EnumDisplayModes callback (hw.dll VA 0x1dc7f10) keeps only modes that are exactly 16:9 (w*9==h*16), 4:3, 5:4 or 16:10 (w*5==h*8), with height >= 480, at the configured bpp. The live ScreenBPP is 32 on all four boxes. AddMode (VA 0x1dc67c0) stops after 32 entries.
GameUI: Options > Video (valve/resource/optionssubvideo.res has a 'Resolution' ComboBox and an 'AspectRatio' ComboBox) lists each mode as '%i x %i'. PrepareResolutionList (gameui.dll VA 0x1003ded0; constants 16.0, 5.0 and 8.0) puts 16:9 and 16:10 modes in the list only when Aspect Ratio is 'Widescreen' (GameUI_AspectWide), and 4:3/5:4 modes only when it is 'Normal'. The constructor preselects Widescreen when the current mode is 16:9 or 16:10, and the aspect combo is enabled only if a widescreen mode exists.
On these boxes the accepted list is 11-14 modes, well under the cap of 32, and it includes 1920x1080 on .123, .145, .195 and .240.

Saved under /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/evidence-1080p/goldsrc-halo/:

- goldsrc_registry_value_matrix.txt: build 4554 reads ScreenWidth/Height/BPP/Windowed, EngineDLL and EngineD3D. It reads no EngineMode* value.

- Staged files read: CounterStrike16/Play Counter-Strike.bat, readme.txt (V42, build 4554, protocol 48), install.reg (ScreenWidth pinned to 800x600), valve/resource/optionssubvideo.res and gameui_english.txt.

titles.fix:
No fix is needed for the menu or the launch.
Recommended cleanup for the later phase:
1. In agent/shared/gameres.h, the CounterStrike16 rows should keep only ScreenWidth, ScreenHeight, ScreenBPP and ScreenWindowed (the values build 4554 actually reads). EngineModeW/H/BPP/Windowed, EngineType and EngineGLDriver are read only by the WON HalfLife1 launcher. Writing them at 1920x1080 plants a mode that engine cannot use.
2. Correct the 'CS ignores -w/-h' and 'one shared value pair' comments in CounterStrike16/install.reg, HalfLife1/install.reg and gameres.h.
3. CounterStrike16/install.reg still pins ScreenWidth to 800x600 (0x320/0x258). That is harmless under the launcher's -w/-h.
titles.fix_source: n/a. The optional cleanup is a repo edit of agent/shared/gameres.h plus comment edits in the staged install.reg files.
titles.fix_risk: None for gameplay: the cleanup only touches registry values the launcher already overrides. Re-verify HalfLife1 and CounterStrike16 once after changing the rule. Resolution is client-local, so there is no effect on the fleet HLDS (protocol 48), the a2s proxies or the BCShield-protected servers.
titles.hw_check:
Use .145 or .123 (XP).
1. `EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\CounterStrike16" "Play Counter-Strike.bat"`.
2. SCREENSHOT 0 should show the VGUI2 main menu at 1920x1080.
3. UICLICK 'Options' (bottom-left, about 63,974 at 1920x1080), open the Video tab, and SCREENSHOT. Expect Aspect Ratio 'Widescreen' and Resolution '1920 x 1080'.
4. UICLICK the Resolution combo and SCREENSHOT the dropdown. Expect 1920 x 1080 alongside 1280 x 720, 1280 x 800, 1440 x 900 and 1680 x 1050 (1600 x 900 on .145/.195).
5. Switch Aspect Ratio to Normal to see the 4:3/5:4 list.
This menu can be driven by the agent: VGUI2 follows the absolute OS cursor, and UIKEY is proven on this build fullscreen.
On .195 (Win7) GDI cannot capture the exclusive surface. Prove fullscreen with DISPLAYCFG get and WINLIST, and view the list in a `-window` relaunch at 1920x1080 (same engine list).
titles.verifier_notes: The 32-entry cap is theoretical here: at most 14 qualifying modes on any LCD box, counted from EnumDisplaySettings. DirectDraw enumerates the same (w,h,bpp) set without refresh duplicates. On .246/.195 the fullscreen join stall recorded in the compat DB is a separate multiplayer issue.

titles.title: Halo
titles.engine: Halo: Combat Evolved PC, Gearbox D3D9 port. halo.exe is 1.10 (FileVersion 01.00.10.0621), the 2014 rebuild installed by Bungie's signed 1.0.10 patch. d3d9.dll is loaded dynamically; config.txt is the card database.
titles.launch_sets:
1920x1080 at 60 Hz, fullscreen. 'Play Halo.bat' runs `call FLEETRES.BAT` and then `halo.exe %HALO_NOVIDEO% -vidmode %FR_W%,%FR_H%,%FR_HZ%`, which gives `-vidmode 1920,1080,60` on all four LCD boxes (FR_HZ is the persisted desktop rate, 60). -vidmode is parsed at VA 0x5168c0 ('%d,%d,%d', defaults 800x600@60) and does not go through the menu list.
Measured: 1920x1080@60 verified on .240 and .246 (now .195) on 2026-08-31. .123 runs at that mode, but GDI caught no frame there.
The 1080-line Keystone overlay files are staged: CONTENT\1080log.ksml, CONTENT\1080editbox.ksml and CONTENT\GALLERY\editbox1080.png. Without them Keystone paints a '404 Error' panel over the 1080p menu.
The mechanism is present and correct: FLEETRES md5 matches the repo and the stager check passes. GAMERES has no rule for Halo, by design (command-line title).
titles.menu_source:
Driver-enumerated, with filters. Settings > Video Setup rebuilds its list each time it opens (VA 0x4baf20 → 0x4bad40 → 0x4baba0). It calls IDirect3D9::EnumAdapterModes for D3DFMT_X8R8G8B8, iterating from the highest index down. A mode is kept only if all of these hold:
- 640 <= w <= 4800 and 480 <= h <= 3600, refresh <= 120 Hz
- not 720x480, 720x576, 848x480 or 848x576
- w <= config.txt MaximumResolution. The staged config.txt sets it for no card; it appears only in the header comment.
- With that default, a VRAM cap: <=32 MB → w<=1024, <=64 MB → w<=1280, <=128 MB → w<=1600, above 128 MB no cap.
- In windowed mode only, w < desktop width and h < desktop height (the flag at 0x71d16c is 1 when neither -window nor -windowed is given).
AddMode (VA 0x4badc0) keeps at most 32 resolutions with up to 8 refresh rates each, taken from the top down.
The fleet LCD cards have 512 MB (.123/.145/.195) and 256 MB (.240), so 1920x1080@60 is listed on all four, in fullscreen.

Saved under /home/voidsstr/development/retro-agent/.claude/evidence-1080p/goldsrc-halo/:

- probe_*.json and probe2_halo2_dirs.json: HWPROFILE VRAM of 512/512/512/256 MB, and the Halo registry. ExitFlag reads 'bad 1' on .123 and 'bad 2' on .145/.240; .145 and .240 also carry Halo's own 'Unknown' card memo keys.

titles.hw_check:
This needs a person at the keyboard. Halo's shell ignores the agent's synthetic keys and absolute clicks: NOTES-halo.txt says so, and the 2026-09-01 .240 windowed frames show a DOWN key moving nothing.
Steps for the person, on .145 or .123 (XP):
1. Launch 'Play Halo.bat' in fullscreen. Do not add -window: in windowed mode every mode at or above the desktop size drops out, so 1920x1080 would vanish from the list.
2. Dismiss the 'did not exit correctly' dialog if it appears (ExitFlag is 'bad 1'/'bad 2' on .123, .145 and .240).
3. Settings > Video Setup > Resolution, and step through to 1920 x 1080.
On the agent side: SCREENSHOT 0 of the fullscreen menu (it worked on XP .240 on 08-31), and `DISPLAYCFG get` should show live 1920x1080 while the game runs. If the list tops out at 1024, 1280 or 1600 wide, Halo's own VRAM detection is the cause, not the driver.
titles.verifier_notes: I did not find the code that writes Halo's VRAM value (0x722bb0), so the VRAM cap is inferred from the cards' real memory (HWPROFILE 256-512 MB). Halo prints the value it detected in its own 'Machine Info' line ('%dM').

titles.title: Halo2
titles.engine: Halo 2 for Windows Vista 1.00.00.11081 (halo2.exe 14,677,368 B, PE 2007-04-30, SubsystemVersion 4.0). It uses D3D9 (Direct3DCreate9Ex when present), Games for Windows LIVE (xlive.dll) and d3dx9_31.
titles.launch_sets:
Nothing in the staged tree sets a mode: no FLEETRES, no GAMERES rule, and install.reg carries only GameInstallDir. halo2.exe has no resolution switch (its only switches are -windowed, -novsync, -nosound, -monitor:, -highquality, -mce, -svu and -hrd). So it runs at its own compiled default, not a per-box mode.
On first run it creates HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Halo 2\Video Settings from a built-in block: 1024x768@60 fullscreen, or a low-spec block of 800x600 (VA 0x864e2c). XP got the low-spec block.
Live values now:
- .123 (XP): 800x600, and the game renders a black window anyway.
- .145 (XP): 800x600.
- .195 (Win7): 1024x768 (verified running at 1024x768 on 09-01).
- .240: the full 4.2 GB tree is present but there is no settings key; the game has never run there.
At startup, validation (VA 0x663597) picks the largest listed mode no larger than ScreenResX x ScreenResY.
How it runs on XP: 'Play Halo 2.bat' copies dwmapi.dll.xpshim to dwmapi.dll and starts `Loader.exe halo2.exe`. Loader redirects the Vista-only ADVAPI32!RegGetValueA import into Wow.dll, which exports RegGetValueA/W and CreateProcessWithTokenW. mf.dll, MFPlat.dll and XTaskDlg.dll are stubs for Media Foundation and TaskDialog. GFWL 1.0.6027 and the DirectX Oct-2006 redist must be installed on each box. On Vista/7, halo2.exe runs directly and the stub must be removed.
titles.menu_source:
A hardcoded whitelist intersected with what the driver offers. halo2.exe VA 0x865010 (file offset 0x465010) holds 10 entries (width, height, aspect class 0=4:3 / 1=16:9 / 2=16:10): 800x600, 1024x768, 1152x720, 1280x720, 1280x960, 1280x1024, 1600x1200, 1680x1050, 1920x1080 (class 1), 1920x1200.
- Fullscreen (VA 0x662bfb): EnumAdapterModes at the desktop format, keeping only whitelist entries, with up to 8 refresh rates each.
- Windowed (DisplayMode 1): all 10 entries, no driver check (VA 0x662f1e returns 10).
The menu (c_resolution_edit_list) shows each as '%dx%d'. With these drivers the fullscreen list is 800x600, 1024x768, 1280x720, 1280x960, 1280x1024, 1680x1050 and 1920x1080; .240 lacks 1680x1050.

titles.fix:
Write the per-box mode into HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Halo 2\Video Settings before launch: ScreenResX=dword %FR_W%, ScreenResY=dword %FR_H%, ScreenRefresh=dword %FR_HZ%, DisplayMode=dword 0.
Mirror it in both places, the way Max Payne and Red Faction already are:
1. Add Halo2 to scripts/fleet/stage-fleetres.py so FLEETRES.EXE/.BAT are staged, with `call "%~dp0FLEETRES.BAT"` plus `FLEETRES.EXE -reg HKCU "Software\Microsoft\Halo 2\Video Settings" <name> dword <v>` lines ahead of the dwmapi/Loader logic.
2. Add GR_OP_REG rows for Halo2 in agent/shared/gameres.h.
Trap: the key has 11 DWORDs (ScreenResX, ScreenResY, ScreenRefresh, AspectRatio, DisplayMode, Brightness, Gamma, AntiAliasing, HudSize, SafeArea, LevelOfDetail). If the key exists but any one of them is missing or not REG_DWORD, the loader (VA 0x663b3e) copies the entire compiled default block over every setting it has already read. A bare two-value write on a box with no key (.240, or any fresh box) therefore still comes up at 1024x768 or 800x600. Write the full block when the key is absent (for example when `reg query ... /v LevelOfDetail` fails), and only the four values above otherwise.
AspectRatio has no reader: the render aspect comes from the whitelist's third column, so setting it to 1 is cosmetic.
titles.fix_source: Already in the repo: FLEETRES.EXE -reg (provisioning/fleetres/fleetres.c, staged in other titles) and the GR_OP_REG writer in gameres.h. Nothing needs downloading.
titles.fix_risk:
Low. These are per-user DWORDs the game writes itself. Worst case, the validator steps down to the largest listed mode, or switches to windowed if nothing fits.
- Frame rate at 1080p is unmeasured on the 8400GS (.145) and the HD 5450 (.195); XP had defaulted to the low-spec block.
- .123 gains nothing until its black-window fault is fixed.
- No multiplayer or anti-cheat effect: GFWL, System Link and the LAN server ignore client resolution.
- The FLEETRES call must not reorder the dwmapi shim / Loader logic in the launcher.
titles.hw_check:
Use .145 (XP, where a D3D9 fullscreen surface can be captured with SCREENSHOT 0) and .195 (Win7).
1. After writing the values, read them back with `REGREAD HKCU Software\Microsoft\Halo 2\Video Settings`.
2. Launch 'Play Halo 2.bat'. `DISPLAYCFG get` should show live 1920x1080, and WINLIST should show 'Halo 2' at 0,0-1920x1080.
3. Main menu > SETTINGS > video > resolution list, viewed in fullscreen. A windowed look proves nothing, because windowed mode lists all 10 whitelist entries without asking the driver.
The menu is keyboard-driven (arrows, Enter/Space for A, Esc for B). Whether the agent's UIKEY reaches its DirectInput8 keyboard is unverified; if it does not, a person has to do it.
On .195, capture with the game's own PrintScreen (My Games\Halo 2\Screenshots) and DOWNLOAD the file, since GDI cannot photograph Win7 exclusive fullscreen.
titles.verifier_notes:
- The low-spec branch on XP is inferred from the live registry (both XP boxes hold exactly the 0x864e2c block). I did not trace the hardware test at 0x663988 to its cause.
- .240 holds the full Halo2 tree even though a note in scripts/fleet/autodeploy.py says .240 is refused Halo 2 for lack of disk space.
- Box state at 2026-09-29 00:09: .240 now reports EDID DELL E2313H (LCD, persisted and live desktop 1920x1080), and HWPROFILE names the active adapter as a Radeon X1600 (0x71C0, 256 MB), not the X800 in the brief. It looks recovered.
